commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Benchmark] Keep bench serve warmups and ready check out of the prefix cache
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

**goal:** `vllm bench serve` warmups and ready check don't prime the prefix cache for the measured run (fixes #66698).

**context:** warmups and the ready check resend request 0, so the first measured request was a cache hit: ttft 67–81 ms instead of ~340 ms.

## Claims

- each warmup and the ready check send a unique `cache_salt`, so they can't create cache hits for each other or the run.
- servers that reject `cache_salt` still work: the ready check retries a probe unsalted when it is rejected as invalid (HTTP 400 or 422); warmups retry unsalted when none succeeded and at least one was rejected. both print a warning. other failures (e.g. a transient 503) keep the salt. `RequestFuncOutput.status_code` records the status.
- `--num-warmups` and `--ready-check-timeout-sec` help text updated.

## Validation

- `test_bench_serve_warmups_do_not_prime_prefix_cache` (new, `--num-warmups 2 --ready-check-timeout-sec 60`): fails on main (`assert 576.0 == 0`) and on this pr's previous head, where only warmups were salted (`assert 192.0 == 0`: the ready check primed request 0); passes here. whole file: 4 passed. (run with `MODEL_NAME` swapped locally to llama-3.1-8b; the 1b repo is gated for me.)
- a100, llama-3.1-8b, 4096-token prompts, 3 warmups: request 0 ttft 67/81 ms on main → 343/329 ms here (348/353 ms with no warmups).
- `test_serve_cache_salt.py` (new, stub server, cpu): a 503 on the first ready check is retried salted (fails on this pr's previous head, which retried unsalted); a 400 on every salted request falls back to unsalted; warmups getting a 503 and a 400 fall back too (fails on the previous head, which needed every warmup rejected).
- fallback: against a fake server that rejects `cache_salt`, the ready check and warmups each fell back to unsalted with a warning, and the run completed 3/3 (server saw 3 salted, 6 unsalted requests).

## Details

- `cache_salt` over `POST /reset_prefix_cache`: no dev-mode server needed, and other clients' cache is untouched.
- not covered: `vllm-rerank` drops `--extra-body`; multimodal encoder caches are keyed without the salt.
- on shared-prefix workloads, warmups no longer warm the shared prefix, same as `--num-warmups 0`.
- not a duplicate. rust counterpart: #66707.
- ai-assisted (metamate). i reviewed every line and ran the tests.

---

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][XPU] Honor user block size for sliding-window layers on XPU
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Build the KV cache layer configs on XPU under the current vllm config, so a user-specified `--block-size` is honored for sliding-window layers. Follow-up to #62656.

## Claims

- On XPU, a user-specified `block_size=16` is now honored for sliding-window layers (e.g. gemma-3). Previously it was silently bumped to 64, which breaks prefix-cache hits below 64 tokens.
- The XPU block-size policy from #62656 is unchanged: without `--block-size` the block size stays 64, and `MultipleOf(16)` is advertised only for a user-specified non-64-multiple size.
- XPU-only change (`XPUWorker`); CUDA/ROCm code paths are untouched.
- Adds a regression test in `test_correctness_sliding_window.py`, which the Intel XPU `v1` CI step already runs.

## Validation

XPU (Arc Pro B60). Before: `upstream/main` @ `c26c9bfeb7`; after: this PR (`9dce47c61a`) on `5e0855d305`.

```bash
cd tests && pytest "v1/e2e/general/test_correctness_sliding_window.py::test_hybrid_sliding_window_honors_user_block_size" -q
```

Before:
```
E       assert 0 == 16
1 failed in 37.64s
```

After:
```
1 passed, 5 deselected in 33.16s
```

The same bug also makes the existing `test_kv_cache_events` fail for gemma-3 (SWA) on XPU. The 32-token request does not fill a 64-token block, so no `BlockStored` event is published. That module is skipped on XPU on main (#66926 enables it), so the skip was disabled locally for this run:

```bash
cd tests && pytest v1/engine/test_engine_core_client.py -k test_kv_cache_events -q
```

Before:
```
kv lcm block sizes 64
E   AssertionError: No message received
FAILED v1/engine/test_engine_core_client.py::test_kv_cache_events[True-tcp-google/gemma-3-1b-it-7]
FAILED v1/engine/test_engine_core_client.py::test_kv_cache_events[False-inproc-google/gemma-3-1b-it-7]
2 failed, 2 passed
```

After:
```
4 passed, 1 skipped, 29 deselected in 75.00s
```

### Default vs. user-specified block size

Checks on XPU with this PR that no `--block-size` keeps 64 and a user-specified size is honored, including for SWA layers.

<details>
<summary>probe.py</summary>

```python
import os, sys
def main():
    os.environ["VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING"] = "0"
    from vllm import LLM
    kw = {} if sys.argv[2] == "none" else {"block_size": int(sys.argv[2])}
    llm = LLM(sys.argv[1], enforce_eager=True, max_model_len=2048,
              gpu_memory_utilization=0.3, **kw)
    bs = llm.llm_engine.vllm_config.cache_config.block_size
    kc = llm.llm_engine.engine_core.engine_core.scheduler.kv_cache_config
    groups = [g.block_size for g in kc.kv_cache_groups]
    print("RESULT", sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], "block_size", bs, "group_block_sizes", groups)
if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```
</details>

```bash
python probe.py google/gemma-3-1b-it none
python probe.py google/gemma-3-1b-it 16
python probe.py meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct none
python probe.py meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct 16
```

```
RESULT google/gemma-3-1b-it none block_size 64 group_block_sizes [64, 64, 64, 64, 64, 64, 64]
RESULT google/gemma-3-1b-it 16 block_size 16 group_block_sizes [16, 16, 16, 16, 16, 16, 16]
RESULT meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct none block_size 64 group_block_sizes [64]
RESULT meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct 16 block_size 16 group_block_sizes [16]
```

On main, `google/gemma-3-1b-it 16` gives all groups 64 (see `kv lcm block sizes 64` above).

## Details

#62656 made XPU FlashAttention's `get_supported_kernel_block_sizes()` read the current vllm config: `MultipleOf(16)` for a user-specified non-64-multiple block size, `MultipleOf(64)` otherwise. Every caller runs under the current config (`load_model`, platform `update_block_size_for_backend`, `initialize_from_config`) except the worker's `get_kv_cache_layer_configs()`. Full-attention layers there take `cache_config.block_size` directly, but sliding-window layers pick their own block via `_largest_kernel_block_within()` -> `get_supported_kernel_block_sizes()`. Without a config they saw only `MultipleOf(64)`, nothing fit the 16-token page budget, the fallback picked 64, and the hybrid KV cache groups were unified to 64.

`XPUWorker` now wraps `get_kv_cache_layer_configs()` in `set_current_vllm_config`, matching `load_model` and `initialize_from_config`:

| | no `--block-size` | `--block-size 16`, non-SWA | `--block-size 16`, SWA |
|---|---|---|---|
| main | 64 | 16 | 64 |
| this PR | 64 | 16 | 16 |

Alternatives considered:
- Wrapping the shared `get_kv_cache_layer_configs()` (earlier revision of this PR) or the SWA branch in `attention.py` also changes CUDA backends that read the current config (e.g. FlashInfer).
- Advertising only `MultipleOf(16)` on XPU (ROCm convention, previous revision) removes the config dependency, but without `--block-size` some heuristics that read only the supported sizes (non-GDN mamba alignment, multi-backend LCM, skip-quant shared page) could pick sizes that are not multiples of 64.

---

commits.pr_title: [Qwen4Exp] Share FP8 PLE tables over NVLink and RDMA
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Share FP8 PLE tables across independently launched Qwen4Exp engines over NVLink or RDMA.

Independent engines otherwise keep separate copies of the same table. Reuse the Engram pool from #67539 so each peer loads only the rows it owns. #68326 covers sharding across DP ranks within one engine.

## Claims

- Two engines sharing the official Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 PLE table hold **23.84 GiB of table data each**. NVLink serves HBM shards, and RDMA serves HBM or pinned host shards.
- Peers validate local row coverage and the FP8 scale before serving. Each peer keeps its own copy of the scale.

## Validation

- **Full model, single-node GB200.** Two TP1/PP1 engines served the official checkpoint with default CUDA Graph capture using NVLink HBM or host RDMA. With either transport, both engines matched all 16 GSM8K response texts from the CPU-offload baseline, and four short probes matched tokens and logprobs. The long-context probe diverged after 12 common generated tokens on NVLink and after 12–21 on host RDMA.
- **Two-node GB200 component test.** Host and HBM RDMA returned exact FP8 rows in eager mode and after CUDA Graph replay with changed IDs. The test used TCPStore for rendezvous.
- **Regression at `f253f2a642`.** Pre-commit and Linux-target mypy passed. The regression used the head's Python and test sources with the build-equivalent `5020556c32` nightly native extensions.

```bash
pytest -q -rs tests/test_config.py tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_ple.py -k 'engram or peer_group or ple'
```

```text
215 passed, 2 skipped, 594 deselected, 22 warnings in 114.21s (0:01:54)
```

`pytest -q -rs tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_reload_lifecycle.py` reported `6 passed in 1.95s`.

<details>
<summary>GB200 lookup latency</summary>

CUDA Graph replay on `e00b32ec10` with 16 IDs per token.

| Setup | Tokens per GPU | Lookup latency |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Two NVLink peers on one GB200 node, official FP8 PLE table in HBM | 8,192 | 31.97 µs p50, 38.11 µs p95 |
| Two GB200 nodes, host RDMA, synthetic 750-row FP8 table with 160 B/row | 16 | ~60 µs p50 |
| Same host RDMA setup | 4,096 | 486–491 µs p50 across peers |

The RDMA timings use 120 samples per peer and batch size.

</details>

## Details

Opt in with TP=1, PP=1, `peer_group_fetch=sync`, and a fresh `peer_group_store` accessible to every engine. Use the same checkpoint and revision throughout the group. Select `peer_group_transport=nvlink` with `cpu_offload=false` for HBM, or `peer_group_transport=rdma` with `cpu_offload=true` for pinned host memory and `false` for HBM. Restart the full group to change weights.

commits.pr_title: [BUG] Fix async EPLB worker shutdown ordering
commits.pr_body:
## 1. Root cause

The async EPLB transfer thread is started as a daemon, but has no explicit
shutdown lifecycle. `Worker.shutdown()` cleans up the model runner and other
resources without stopping or joining that thread.

A daemon thread exits when its process exits, not when `Worker.shutdown()`
returns. It can therefore remain blocked on `rearrange_event` or on a pending
layer result while worker cleanup proceeds.

## 2. Fix

Add `EplbState.stop_async_loop()` and call it at the beginning of
`Worker.shutdown()`, before resource cleanup:

1. Drain any in-flight async EPLB results using the existing `drain_async()`.
   Acknowledge each result without applying its transferred weights, allowing
   the background thread to finish the current cycle.
2. Set a stop event and record `rearrange_event` to wake the thread.
3. Check the stop event after waking, exit instead of starting another cycle,
   and join the thread before continuing cleanup.

Clear the stop event when starting a new async worker. If no async worker
exists, stopping is a no-op.

## 3. Behavior without the fix

With async EPLB enabled, calling worker shutdown does not terminate the EPLB
thread. If the worker process remains alive, the thread can retain references
to the EPLB state and model resources after model-runner cleanup.

If shutdown happens during a rebalance, the thread can still be transferring
experts or waiting for the main thread to consume a layer result. Subsequent
distributed teardown can then overlap with unfinished EPLB work.

Normal process exit eventually terminates the daemon thread and reclaims
process resources. This change establishes a clean shutdown order; it does
not claim that ordinary vLLM exit always crashes or hangs.

The added two-rank `LLM.generate()` regression checks that shutdown removes the
model and stops the async worker. Its long rebalance interval exercises the
idle-worker case, not an in-flight transfer. Pre-commit hooks passed; the GPU
regression has not been run in this session.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Restore HY4 Flash CUDA platform checks
commits.pr_body:
## Root cause
The failure was introduced by [vllm-project/vllm#69013](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/69013) (`1bdc437402`), which removed `validate_runtime()` and its calls from the HY4 Flash text and multimodal constructors. This also removed the explicit rejection of non-CUDA platforms. On AMD, initialization now enters the NVIDIA implementation and fails in `FlashCompressedIndexer` with `RuntimeError: Flash IndexPool requires DeepGEMM paged MQA`, instead of the `NotImplementedError` required by the existing initialization test.

Pre-merge coverage missed this case: [Buildkite 104917](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/104917) ran the AMD small-subset initialization job, but did not run AMD Extra Initialization, which selects `test_can_initialize_large_subset[HYV4DFlyModel]`. The main-branch run in Buildkite 104931 exercised that job and exposed the regression.

Restore the platform check at both NVIDIA model entry points, before constructing the backbone or indexer. This preserves the existing unsupported-platform contract without restoring the unrelated configuration checks removed by the cleanup.

## Overview

Fix the AMD `HYV4DFlyModel` initialization failure in [Buildkite 104931](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/104931/list?jid=01a1ff97-56aa-4194-8faf-39315a39f130&tab=output).

## Claims

Reject non-CUDA initialization of the NVIDIA HY4 Flash implementation with `NotImplementedError("HYV4 Flash requires NVIDIA CUDA")`, as required by the existing test. Only the text and multimodal model files change; CUDA initialization behavior and CI configuration remain unchanged.

commits.pr_title: [Kernel] Let --linear-backend deep_gemm override the DeepGemm model a…
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

On Blackwell, vLLM turns off DeepGEMM for the FP8 linear layers of Qwen3.5 because of the GSM8K accuracy drop reported in #37804 and #38083. No option turns it back on.

I measured Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-FP8 on one B200, and the drop seems to come from thinking. `gsm8k_eval.py` sends a plain-text prompt without the chat template. With this prompt, the model opens a `<think>` block in almost every response. With DeepGEMM, the model reasons inside the block more often: in 313 responses per run, against 196 with vLLM's default settings. Much of this reasoning hits the 256-token output limit or a stop string before the model gives an answer. Answers that do finish within the token limit are about 96.5% correct with or without DeepGEMM.

With the chat template and thinking off, I saw no real difference. [lm-eval](https://github.com/EleutherAI/lm-evaluation-harness)'s `gsm8k`  scored all three servers I tested within 0.7 points of each other.

So users should have a way to turn DeepGEMM back on for these models. With this PR, `--linear-backend deep_gemm` overrides vLLM's choice and logs a warning.

## Claims

1. **The default does not change.** Without an explicit request, vLLM still turns DeepGEMM off for the listed model types, and the warning now says how to turn it back on.
2. **An explicit request turns DeepGEMM back on.** Either `--linear-backend deep_gemm` or `deep_gemm` for `fp8_block_w8a8` in `linear_backend_per_quant` works. The per-quantization setting wins.
3. **The config and the kernel agree.** `quant_config.use_deep_gemm` stays `True`, so weight dequantization expects DeepGEMM's layout.
4. **The GSM8K drop comes from thinking.** DeepGEMM tips a near tie after `<think>` toward reasoning, which often doesn't finish within the output limit. Answers that finish are equally accurate (see Details).

## Validation

  Servers:

  ```bash
  # Default: DeepGEMM stays off for the FP8 linear layers
  vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-FP8 --port 8000 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-model-len 4096

  # Opt-in
  vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-FP8 --port 8000 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-model-len 4096 \
      --linear-backend deep_gemm

Measurements, three runs of each on each server:

  ```bash
  python3 tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000

  lm_eval --model local-chat-completions \
      --model_args model=Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-FP8,base_url=http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/chat/completions,num_concurrent=64,tokenizer_backend=none \
      --tasks gsm8k --apply_chat_template \
      --gen_kwargs '{"max_gen_toks": 256, "chat_template_kwargs": {"enable_thinking": false}}'
  ```

  | Server | `gsm8k_eval.py` | lm-eval `gsm8k` |
  |---|---|---|
  | Default | 0.788 / 0.775 / 0.786 | 0.901 / 0.901 / 0.898 |
  | `--linear-backend deep_gemm` | 0.751 / 0.745 / 0.739 |  0.901 / 0.901 / 0.905 |

## Details

These measurements used vLLM v0.28.0, which is older than this branch. For the DeepGEMM server, I modified the v0.28.0 source code to remove the model types from the auto-disable list. The run of this branch in Validation shows the same pattern: a drop with the plain-text prompt, and none with the chat template. So the version does not change the conclusion.

### Setup

- `Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-FP8` on one B200, vLLM v0.28.0, BF16 KV cache, default scheduler limits.
- Three servers. All run the MoE experts with `FLASHINFER_TRTLLM`, and differ in the linear layers and in where E8M0 scales are used:

  | Server | Linear layers | E8M0 scales |
  |---|---|---|
  | Default | CUTLASS | MoE inputs |
  | DeepGEMM | DeepGEMM | MoE inputs and linear layers |
  | `VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=0` | CUTLASS | None |

- Every check runs the 1,319 test questions 5-shot with greedy decoding, three times on each server.
- The probe is my script for looking inside `gsm8k_eval.py`'s score, which reports only the total. The probe imports that script's prompts, output limit, stop strings, and answer extraction, and sends the same requests. It saves every response with the two most likely tokens at each step and their log-probabilities. These show how each response ended, and how close greedy decoding came to choosing the other token.

### Accuracy

Mean of three runs, with the lowest and highest in parentheses.

| Check | `VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=0` | Default | DeepGEMM |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `gsm8k_eval.py` | 80.0% (79.4–81.1) | 79.8% (78.2–81.4) | 71.1% (70.7–71.7) |
| Probe | 80.9% (80.4–81.3) | 78.9% (78.2–79.9) | 71.0% (70.0–72.1) |
| Probe, 1,024 tokens | 85.6% (85.4–86.1) | 84.9% (83.5–85.7) | 75.3% (74.8–76.0) |
| lm-eval `gsm8k` | 90.0% (89.8–90.1) | 90.7% (90.4–90.9) | 90.2% (89.5–90.7) |

- `gsm8k_eval.py` and the probe send the same plain-text prompt, with a 256-token output limit unless noted.
- lm-eval uses the chat template with thinking off.

### Where the answers are lost

Answers that finish are 96–97% correct on every server. DeepGEMM loses accuracy because more of its responses never finish. The probe's responses, averaged over three runs:

| Server | Reasoned | Empty block | No `<think>` | Cut off | Stopped while thinking | Ended | Accuracy of ended |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=0` | 163 | 1,153 | 3 | 188 | 47 | 1,084 | 96.5% |
| Default | 196 | 1,122 | 1 | 204 | 58 | 1,057 | 96.5% |
| DeepGEMM | 313 | 1,003 | 3 | 256 | 122 | 941 | 96.8% |
| `VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=0`, 1,024 tokens | 163 | 1,153 | 3 | 109 | 54 | 1,156 | 95.9% |
| Default, 1,024 tokens | 173 | 1,146 | 0 | 107 | 61 | 1,151 | 96.2% |
| DeepGEMM, 1,024 tokens | 322 | 995 | 2 | 158 | 158 | 1,003 | 96.0% |

The first three columns count what the response did after `<think>`. The next three count how it ended. Each group adds up to 1,319.

- **Reasoned**: wrote text inside the thinking block.
- **Empty block**: wrote `<think>`, a blank line, and `</think>`, then answered.
- **Cut off**: hit the output limit.
- **Stopped while thinking**: wrote `Question`, one of `gsm8k_eval.py`'s stop strings, before closing the block.
- **Ended**: finished the answer, nearly always with `<|endoftext|>` right after `#### N`.

Compared with the default server, DeepGEMM reasoned in 117 more responses per run, left 116 more unfinished, and got 104 fewer correct. With 1,024 tokens, it still left 148 more unfinished.

### Why DeepGEMM reasons more often

The probe saves the log-probabilities of the two most likely tokens at every step. At the token right after `<think>`, those two are `\n\n`, which leads to an empty block and an answer, and `\n`, which starts reasoning. For each question, the gap is log p(`\n\n`) − log p(`\n`), in nats. A positive gap means the model answers at once, and a negative gap means it reasons.

1. **The choice is nearly a tie.** Across all questions and runs, the gap was never larger than 0.625 nats in either direction, and most reasoning started from an exact tie.
2. **DeepGEMM moves the gap toward reasoning.** Pairing each question across a default run and a DeepGEMM run, the gap is about 0.055 nats lower on average with DeepGEMM, in every run pair. Between two runs of the same server, the average change is 0.006 nats or less.
3. **That token is where the runs split.** Most questions that the default server answered correctly and DeepGEMM did not, 230 of 251, first differed at the token right after `<think>`.
4. **lm-eval never reaches this choice.** With the chat template and thinking off, the prompt already ends with a closed `<think></think>` block.

commits.pr_title: [Recipe] Kimi-K3.1-Pro: MI355X kimi-k31-712d9eb image and released DSpark draft, align with InferenceX#5119
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Align the Kimi-K3.1-Pro MI355X AgentX TP8 preset (`mi355x_agentx`) with [InferenceX #5119](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/5119) (`kimik3.1-fp4-mi355x-vllm-agentic-dspark`). #5119 makes these changes:
- It moves the lane to the `kimi-k31-712d9eb` image, the head of [`k31-amd-tracking`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/tree/k31-amd-tracking).
- It switches to the released DSpark draft.
- It sets the prefix-match unit to the KV block span.
- It runs 4 draft tokens from concurrency 16 to 48.

## Claims

- **Image.**
  - The preset pins `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:kimi-k31-712d9eb@sha256:7c167350f127a3019ac2c2fc99f6d3229356e8e8e033a7634c3201f072f0ecf4`, the digest #5119 measured.
  - The recipe-level AMD `docker_image` moves from `kimi-k31-5c14fe8` to `kimi-k31-712d9eb`.
- **Draft.** `--speculative-config` pins `revision: e4e6e6261e9f8b6d5f249f9627eb6b109d762d5f` of `Inferact/Kimi-K3.1-Pro-DSpark`, the revision InferenceX's golden acceptance lengths were measured with.
  - From concurrency 16, the draft also gets `kv_cache_dtype: fp8`, next to the feature's `TRITON_ATTN`. Without it, the image's `configure_dense_draft` gives the draft a BF16 (`auto`) KV cache.
  - At concurrency 1 and 4, `attention_backend` and `kv_cache_dtype` are removed (`null`). The image then picks `KIMI_K3_FLYDSL_SWA_GQA` with a BF16 draft cache, as InferenceX ran it.
- **Prefix-match unit.** `--prefix-match-unit` is 1152 (it was 64), the attention block span under DCP8. Concurrency 1 (no DCP, 1280-token blocks) sets 1280.
- **Block size.** The preset removes the Spec decoding feature's `--block-size 1152`, as InferenceX ran it. K3.1 sizes its own packed block on this image: 1152 under DCP8 and 1280 without DCP.
- **Draft tokens.** Concurrency 32 and 48 run 4 draft tokens; they ran 3. The capture sizes move to multiples of 5:
  - Concurrency 32: 5 to 100.
  - Concurrency 48: 5 to 240, covering 48 × (1 + 4) rows.
  - Both keep the prefill sizes up to 10240.
- **Source.** The preset's source is now InferenceX #5119 at `2bf834d5`.
- **Runbook.**
  - **KV capacity:** 3.2M tokens at concurrency 1, 18.1M at concurrency 4.
  - **New `--prefix-match-unit` bullet.**
  - **SP prefill:** now active at every point, including concurrency 1.
  - **Draft attention:** the draft's backend and KV dtype at each point, and why `VLLM_K31_BEAT_CTXKV` needs the BF16 draft cache.
  - **Image switches:** the new image-only switches.
  - **Results:** run 44640765021.
  - **Synthetic acceptance:** the golden ALs for the released draft (4.16 / 3.81 / 3.46 for 7 / 5 / 4 tokens).

## Validation

From a `vllm-project/recipes` checkout at `d33e7b7`, with this branch as the `vllm` source:

```bash
node scripts/validate-source.mjs --source vllm --dir "$VLLM_CHECKOUT/recipes"
node --test scripts/test-guide-html.mjs scripts/test-presets.mjs scripts/test-schema.mjs
typos recipes/models/moonshotai/Kimi-K3.1-Pro.yaml   # typos v1.51.1
```

- The source validator passes.
- 49 of 49 renderer tests pass.
- `typos` passes.

**JSON API diff.** I built the JSON API on `main` and on this branch. Both have the same 23,649 files, and 8 of them differ, all under `moonshotai/Kimi-K3.1-Pro`:
- `presets/mi355x_agentx.json`: the preset changes above.
- `Kimi-K3.1-Pro.json`: the same preset changes, plus the runbook and guide text and `model.docker_image.amd`.
- `hw/mi355x.json` and five `hw/mi355x/strategies/*.json` files: only the image tag, because the recipe-level AMD image changed.

**Comparison with InferenceX.** I compared the six rendered points flag by flag with #5119's `agentic.yaml` (base merged with each concurrency override). Every point's arguments, JSON configs and environment match. The only exception is the harness flag `--served-model-name`, which the preset leaves out.

**GPU evidence.** This PR adds no new GPU run. The evidence is [InferenceX run 44640765021](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/44640765021) at `2bf834d5`, which passed all six performance points (one run each) and GSM8K at four concurrencies. The table includes the previous numbers from #67817 (run 43717568009, `kimi-k31-5c14fe8`, preview draft) for comparison.

| Concurrency | Interactivity p50 / p90 (tokens/s/user) | Total tokens/s per GPU | Previous p90 / tokens/s per GPU | GSM8K strict EM (1,319) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 337.5 / 328.9 | 2,539 | 255.1 / 2,164 | 0.979 |
| 4 | 244.0 / 211.5 | 3,493 | 169.7 / 3,137 | 0.980 |
| 16 | 114.0 / 91.5 | 9,811 | 85.3 / 9,089 | – |
| 24 | 93.5 / 77.9 | 14,658 | 69.6 / 13,387 | – |
| 32 | 81.0 / 70.0 | 17,348 | 59.5 / 15,850 | 0.980 |
| 48 | 47.6 / 30.3 | 22,240 | 26.9 / 20,319 | 0.980 |

Throughput points use synthetic acceptance at the golden AL of the new draft. The previous numbers used the preview draft's lower ALs, so the throughput comparison is not like for like.

## Details

**Not a duplicate.** This updates the preset that #67600 added and #67817 last aligned. No other open Kimi-K3.1-Pro recipe PR changes this preset; the others target other hardware or the block size on the Day 0 image.

**Image-only switches.** vLLM main reads none of the new switches: `VLLM_SWA_FINE_GRAINED_PREFIX_HITS`, `VLLM_K31_DRAFT_FLYDSL_ATTN` and `VLLM_K31_BEAT_CTXKV`. Main also has no `KIMI_K3_FLYDSL_SWA_GQA` backend, and it defaults a GQA draft to `FLASH_ATTN`, which fails on ROCm. The runbook says so.

**Checked against the new server logs and source.**
- `Setting attention block size to 1280` without DCP and `1152` under DCP8.
- `kv lcm block sizes`: 1280 without DCP and 9216 under DCP8.
- Concurrency 1: `Using KIMI_K3_FLYDSL_SWA_GQA backend`, CTXKV in one launch for 5 layers, 16 DSA splits, and `headroom 8.0 GiB`.
- Concurrency 4: the same draft backend, and the fused Markov sampling off with more than one request.
- From concurrency 16: `TRITON_ATTN` for the draft.
- `configure_dense_draft` ([`dense_draft.py`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/712d9eb37f9fe0282cb23c9de94381fbce03085a/vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/dense_draft.py#L41-L58)) only fills draft fields the user left unset. That is why the fp8 draft KV cache from concurrency 16 has to be explicit.

**Not re-measured.** InferenceX kept `--prefix-match-unit` at the block span and did not re-measure a 64-token unit on this image. The image adds fine-grained sliding-window prefix hits, so 64 may no longer cost anything there.

AI assistance was used (Claude Opus 5.5, `claude-opus-5-5`, via Claude Code): it drafted the change, ran the validation above, compared the rendered commands with the InferenceX recipe, and checked the runbook against the image's source and the InferenceX server logs. The submitter reviewed the changes.

## Overview

Add Nemotron Shortcut (text, MTP draft head, image and video inputs) as one self-contained package, `vllm/models/nemotron_shortcut/`, in the per-model layout of `vllm/models/kimi_k3/` and `vllm/models/glm5next/` (RFC #42770).

Depends on [#67941](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/67941) (layer-compact KV layout with mixed page sizes) and [#68353](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/68353) (MXFP8 linear layers with unaligned N). This PR has only the model, which needs #67941 to run and #68353 for MXFP8 weights.

## Claims

- Text, image and video inputs; TP, PP, DP + EP, MTP; BF16, MXFP8 and NVFP4 weights; BF16, FP8 and NVFP4 (pending FlashInfer bump) KV cache.
- The config and the image processor are the checkpoint's own, loaded with `--trust-remote-code`; vLLM adds none.
- The model's parts live in the model directory: SDSA sparse attention (an indexer selects each query's Top-K keys, an MQA core attends to them), the Gated DeltaProduct (GDP) mixer, and the shortcut MoE (routed experts read the block input, so dispatch can start before the mixer runs).
- Outside the model directory, vLLM only registers the model (table below). No model runner, scheduler or KV cache manager changes beyond [#67941](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/67941).

## Validation

One node of 4x GB300; torch 2.14, transformers 5.22.2, vLLM's bundled FlashAttention 4; vLLM's compiled extensions from the wheel of `main` `4fdc79d89d`, Python from this branch with #67941 and #68353 applied.

**Unit tests**

```bash
pytest tests/models/nemotron_shortcut tests/v1/core tests/v1/worker/test_mamba_hybrid_model_state.py
```

**1496 passed, 1 failed** (55 min). The failure is on `main` too: `tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_planning.py::test_finalize_extensible_kv_cache_auto_max_model_len_warns_when_short[True]`.

**Review fixes** (9b5ec991: fp32 streams across PP stages, multimodal MTP inputs), with FlashInfer 0.7.4 (vLLM's pin):

```bash
pytest tests/models/nemotron_shortcut
```

**165 passed, 1 skipped**: the NVFP4-experts test in `moe/test_moe.py` needs FlashInfer's `routing_weights_before_fc2`. The new `test_pp_engine.py` fails on the previous head (53bd4208) with the receiving stage's bf16 buffers.

**Checkpoint config and processor** (f1d9e9f9): served with `--trust-remote-code`, a BF16 checkpoint gives the same gsm8k accuracy and MTP acceptance as with vLLM's own copies, and the same prompt tokens for image and video requests. `--hf-overrides` still sets the `sdsa_*` settings. `pytest tests/models/nemotron_shortcut`, whose tiny models now load a stand-in config as remote code: **165 passed, 1 skipped**, as before.

## Details

```text
vllm/models/nemotron_shortcut/
    nvidia/
        model.py        language model: GDP, MLP, attention and shortcut-MoE blocks, wide residual
        gdp.py          GDP mixer on FlashInfer's GDP kernels, its state layout, head-wise TP
        mlp.py          dense MLP with the soft-clamped squared ReLU
        mtp.py          MTP draft head (one repeated block)
        vision.py       Pixtral vision tower + projector; video tubelets of T frames
        sdsa/           SDSA layer, backends (BF16/FP8/NVFP4 K/V), prefill planning, KV cache grouping
        moe/            router, staged runner (with the DP all-gather/reduce-scatter overlap), experts
```

Size: 7,610 lines in the model directory, 1,913 in tests, 68 outside the model directory (registrations below and the CI job).

| Outside the model directory | Why |
|---|---|
| `vllm/model_executor/models/registry.py`, `tests/models/registry.py` | the model and its MTP draft head |
| `vllm/config/speculative.py` | `nemotron_shortcut_mtp` in `MTPModelTypes`; the draft keeps the checkpoint's `quantization_config`, as Kimi K3's and GLM-5.3-Flash's MTP do |
| `vllm/config/compilation.py` | `vllm::nemotron_shortcut_gdp` and `vllm::nemotron_shortcut_sdsa_indexer` as default splitting ops |
| `vllm/v1/attention/backends/registry.py` | `NEMOTRON_SHORTCUT_SDSA` in `AttentionBackendEnum`, as other model-driven backends |
| `.buildkite/test_areas/models_basic.yaml` | CI job |

Design:

- **SDSA**: K is the checkpoint's `index_topk`; the other settings (`sdsa_*`) are "auto" unless set with `--hf-overrides`. Each indexer cache joins its core's KV cache group, which needs #67941's layout fix.
- **MoE**: a model-local `MoERunner` stages begin/run/finish and, with DP, overlaps the all-gather and reduce-scatter with the mixer and the shared experts. The experts apply the soft clamp `relu2(c * tanh(x / c))`.
- **GDP**: FlashInfer's `gdp_prefill` for prefill, `cake_gdp` for decode and MTP verification.

## Overview

DFlash/DFlash2 now accept draft checkpoints with `sample_from_anchor: true` (anchor-first layout: `K` queries for `K` draft tokens) instead of rejecting them at startup. The default fill-in layout (`1 + K` queries) is unchanged.

**Supersedes #54154.** This is the same change as @qianlihuang's #54154, rebased onto main's `SpeculatorConfig` classes (#63205); #54154 no longer applies to main. @qianlihuang is credited as co-author on the main commit. Two parts of #54154 are no longer needed on main:
- **V1-runner rejection:** the V1 GPU model runner has been removed, and only the V2 runner (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu`) runs DFlash.
- **Scheduler drafting-slot tweak in `SpeculativeConfig`:** main now delegates this to `SpeculatorConfig.max_num_new_slots_for_drafting`. DFlash leaves it at 0 because it drafts in a separate query pass, so the query layout doesn't affect it. KV lookahead, the part that does depend on the layout, is handled here through `DFlashSpeculatorConfig.num_lookahead_tokens`.

## Claims

- **Problem:** `DFlashSpeculator.__init__` raises `ValueError: sample_from_anchor=True is not supported for DFlash` for any checkpoint whose `dflash_config` sets `sample_from_anchor: true`, e.g. the public `DaoCloud/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2-Exp`. The DFlash input kernel already supports both layouts through its `SAMPLE_FROM_ANCHOR` path; only the config/allocation side hardcoded `1 + K`.
- **Fix:** `DFlashSpeculatorConfig` reads `sample_from_anchor` from the checkpoint's `dflash_config`, falling back to the top-level config key (default `False`; a `ValueError` if the two disagree), and exposes one query width, `num_query_tokens` (`K` anchor-first, `1 + K` fill-in). The speculator, KV lookahead and the DFlash2 grouped-conv block size all use it. DSpark already used the anchor-first layout, so it now inherits the same logic and only overrides its default (`True`).
- No new flags, env vars or config fields. The layout comes from the checkpoint.

| | before (main) | after (this PR) |
|---|---|---|
| `DaoCloud/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2-Exp` (anchor-first), GSM8K / acceptance length | `ValueError` at startup | 0.920 / 6.03 |
| `z-lab/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2` (fill-in), acceptance rate / length, 128 prompts | 0.7376 / 6.163 | 0.7376 / 6.163 (128/128 identical outputs) |
| Anchor-first DFlash2 deployment (Qwen3-Omni ASR, private draft), output identity vs the same draft served through an out-of-tree patch, greedy, concurrency 1 | — | 4,090 / 4,096 = 99.85% byte-identical |
| Same deployment, acceptance rate (patch → this PR) | 0.5148 | 0.5139 |
| Same deployment, served RPS / P99 at 95 RPS offered (patch → this PR) | 77.55 / 319.9 ms | 77.49 / 318.9 ms |

Run-to-run baseline for the identity row: two identical runs of the out-of-tree-patch control on the same GPU driver matched on 4,094 / 4,096 outputs, with 2 differing among clips valid in both runs. Changing the NVIDIA driver alone (610.57.04 → 620.70.06, same code) changed about 900 outputs and moved acceptance to 0.50, so only same-driver pairs are compared here.

## Details

- **Why the config class:** #63205 moved per-method geometry (lookahead, drafting slots, hidden-state needs) into `SpeculatorConfig` subclasses, so query width belongs in `DFlashSpeculatorConfig` rather than in `SpeculativeConfig` helpers as in #54154. One property drives allocation, lookahead, warmup and the DFlash2 conv block, so they can't drift apart, which was the concern raised in #48909 and #59105. In the #59105 review, @benchislett noted there was no fundamental reason to support `sample_from_anchor` only for DSpark and not for DFlash; this PR makes both use the same property.
- **Default is unchanged:** checkpoints without the flag keep `1 + K`. DSpark keeps its anchor-first default.
- **Compatibility:** no kernel changes. The Triton input-prep kernel already takes `SAMPLE_FROM_ANCHOR` as a constexpr, so CUDA graphs and `torch.compile` see the same shapes as DSpark anchor-first. Attention backends are unaffected. ROCm segmented attention still sizes for `K + 1`, which is a safe upper bound for anchor-first. Speculators-format DFlash checkpoints already map `sample_from_anchor` into `dflash_config` (`transformers_utils/configs/speculators/algos.py`), so they get the same behaviour; the flag defaults to `False` there too.
- **Docs:** adds a "DFlash query layouts" section to `docs/features/speculative_decoding/README.md`.
- **CI:** the new unit tests run in the existing V1 Spec Decode step, which covers all of `tests/v1/spec_decode`. The anchor-first e2e case goes in the existing DFlash e2e file.

### Overlapping open PRs

These PRs edit the same files. Whichever lands second needs a rebase:
- #63532 (AdaFlash length heads) edits the lines next to the removed `ValueError` in `DFlashSpeculator.__init__`, and checks the checkpoint `block_size` against `1 + K`.
- #66612 (narrow the draft block under dynamic SD) makes the DFlash2 conv block size a runtime value and narrows the query pass to `1 + K`. With this PR, the anchor-first width would be `K`.
- #65130 (draft token heads) changes the `DFlashSpeculator` constructor.
- #68620 (draft dtype) adds `supported_options` to `DFlashSpeculatorConfig`.

### Anticipated review questions

- **Why not detect the layout from other checkpoint keys (`deepspec`, `draft_output_offset`, `block_size`)?** The checkpoint already declares `sample_from_anchor`, and #48639 established that flag as the contract. Sniffing other keys would be fragile.
- **Does this change existing DFlash deployments?** No. The flag defaults to `False`, and the z-lab fill-in run gives identical outputs and acceptance before and after.
- **Why touch DSpark?** DSpark already had its own copy of the anchor-first query-width and lookahead logic. It now uses the shared property and only overrides its default, so its behaviour is unchanged (`tests/v1/worker/test_dspark_utils.py` passes).
- **Is there a public reproducer?** Yes: `DaoCloud/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2-Exp` fails at startup on main and is now an e2e test case.
